description: Canonical Fig. 7 organized-versus-unorganized RI comparison driven by the same localized active-adenylyl-cyclase disk source.
notes: Resting free cAMP is 25 nM in both conditions.
The common source is a 0.1-um-radius membrane disk containing 50 active AC molecules, each producing 100 cAMP molecules/s, for a total source rate of 5000 cAMP molecules/s.
The script derives the uniform disk flux density from AC production and source area rather than imposing a source concentration.
With D_free = 100 um^2/s, the AC source produces a source-surface free-cAMP concentration near 0.289 uM and a common input near 0.242 uM at 20 nm from the source.
The identical 20-nm proximal waveform drives both downstream transport formulations for 1 s and returns to the common 25-nM background afterward.
Downstream transport is the controlled difference: radially symmetric 3D conventional buffered diffusion versus reduced structured-buffered mobility D_relay(c).
PDE-mediated clearance acts on the evoked component, -k_clear*(c-c_rest), preserving the common resting background.
Local PKAc release is non-depleting: R_PKAc = k_rel*f_AB^2*H_T, H_T = RT/rho_R_to_C.
The apparent attenuation length and latency-vs-distance-squared fit are descriptive summaries, not fundamental constants.
